learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed Recording.
Apply Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed Recording to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Posterior alpha commonly increases with relaxed eye closure and attenuates with eye opening. Repeated blocks help assess reproducibility and vigilance.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Eye closure also changes ocular artifact and arousal. Lack of alpha blocking is nonspecific and should not be over-interpreted without context.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Controlled blocks improve routine interpretation and qEEG reliability.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Analysing mixed eyes-open and eyes-closed segments against a single normative condition invalidates comparison.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed Recording?
options: Posterior alpha commonly increases with relaxed eye closure and attenuates with eye opening. Repeated blocks help assess reproducibility and vigilance.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Posterior alpha commonly increases with relaxed eye closure and attenuates with eye opening. Repeated blocks help assess reproducibility and vigilance.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed Recording?

Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder

reviewPrompts.answer: Eye closure also changes ocular artifact and arousal. Lack of alpha blocking is nonspecific and should not be over-interpreted without context.
